column1: # tools/copy-ban-list.tsv -- the ONE ban list.
# Read by tools/check-copy-banned-terms.sh (this repo) and, byte for byte, by
# BUZZ desktop/scripts/check-copy-banned-terms.mjs. The parity test
# (16-INVARIANT-TESTS.md section 6.2) asserts both produce identical verdicts
# over tools/fixtures/copy-corpus/, so this file is the only place a ban is
# added, softened or scoped.
# Source of truth for the bans themselves: APPENDIX-NORMATIVE.md section 7
# ("Banned outright in rendered strings") plus the vocabulary table above it.
# A row here that the appendix does not carry is a brief amendment, not a
# convenience.
# COLUMNS, tab-separated:
#   id        stable slug. Appears in the failure output and is the allowlist key.
#   severity  P0 | P1 | hygiene. Reported; does not change the exit code -- every
#             row fails the build. Severity tells a reviewer how hard to think.
#   flags     'i' = case-insensitive (pattern must then be written lowercase);
#             '-' = case-sensitive.
#   minlen    minimum length of the extracted string before the row applies.
#             '0' for almost everything; 4 for the exclamation-mark rule, whose
#             appendix wording is "any rendered string longer than three
#             characters".
#   pattern   POSIX ERE, matched against ONE extracted rendered string.
#             awk's ERE has no \b, so a word boundary is written
#             `(^|[^a-z])word([^a-z]|$)`. Five rows need it and the fixture
#             proves each: without it `release` trips bare-lease, `control-plane`
#             trips bare-lane, `resources` trips bare-source-count and `hunting`
#             trips hunt-noun. All four were live false positives on this
#             repository's own assets on the first real run.
#   exempt    POSIX ERE. If it also matches the same string, the hit is dropped.
#             '-' = no exemption. Matched against the SAME normalized string as
#             `pattern` (lowercased when flags=i), so an exemption written for a
#             case-insensitive row must itself be lowercase.
#   message   what to write instead. Printed verbatim on failure.
# WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHY
#   1. 'signed'/'verified' on a finding, escalation, hold, containment-lease or
#      bare response-receipt card (appendix section 7) is NOT a row. That ban is
#      card-scoped and a flat string scan cannot see which card a string lands
#      on. It is enforced instead by the DOM assertion in
#      tests/playwright/perch-provenance.spec.ts (INV-25), which reads the seven
#      card presenters directly. Putting it here would produce a false FAIL on
#      "the daemon signed the release attestation", which is true and renderable,
#      and would still miss "verified" reaching a finding card through a variable.
#   2. NOTHING HERE COVERS A STRING THAT ARRIVES AS DATA. The scanner reads
#      authored literals: copy-module strings, four attribute values, six object
#      field names, and JSX text nodes. A daemon-supplied string interpolated
#      into a rendered slot is invisible to every row below, in every case. The
#      `approve` row's exemption exists precisely because the daemon's own hold
#      reason is such a string and render law 1's fourth slot REQUIRES it be
#      rendered. Daemon-supplied text is INV-14's problem (the AdversaryText
#      brand and <AdversaryString>), not this file's, and 16-INVARIANT-TESTS.md
#      section 7.7 states the limit so a green line here is not read as coverage.
id
approve
column7: Perch does not authorize. Render law 6: the control says "record my decision and send it to the daemon". EXEMPTION: the daemon's own verbatim policy reason is "authorized but held for human approval" (AMB crates/swarm-policy/src/static_gate.rs:297, set by StaticApprovalGate::evaluate inside swarm_detect --serve and carried onto every PolicyDecision and thus onto B1's HoldRationale). Render law 1's fourth slot requires it be rendered verbatim, and 12-BACKEND-BILL-API.md commits it as part of B1's record. Quoting the daemon is not the product claiming an authority.

column1: deny-label
column7: Capital-D Deny is policy's typed word; the operator's word is Refuse. Lowercase mono `deny` as a wire value is fine.

column1: trust-claim
column7: No trust anchor exists. Say "attestation matches this body". WORD-BOUNDED, and the boundary idiom is not enough on its own: awk's `[^a-z]` treats a hyphen as a boundary, so `repeat-proof` and `future-proof` still matched. The exempt column carries the hyphenated-compound form explicitly, which is reviewable in a way that loosening the boundary class would not be -- `lane` genuinely wants a hyphen to be a boundary, so the two rows cannot share one rule. Found by scanning this artifact set's own test names.

column1: shield-glyph
column7: No shield or lock glyph beside an attestation (appendix section 7). Severity is a word plus a four-segment bar, never a glyph.

column1: quorum-fraction
column7: Committee of one. Render "committee of 1 (solo transport)".

column1: bare-source-count
column7: Render law 2: never a bare source count. Always "N sources / M agents".

column1: reassurance
column5: everything looks good|all clear|you.{0,3}re all caught up|no data|nothing to see
column7: Voice law L6. An empty queue is a claim about coverage; name what is not covered.

column1: hunt-noun
column7: 'hunt' is dropped as a noun (06 section 3). The noun is "case"; the field label hunt_id and the identifier tokens hunt-evt-1 / hunt_id survive (22-DEMO-FIXTURE.md amendment C-A1).

column1: clowder
legacy-codename
product-codename
column7: The product is Ambush; Perch is an internal codename (00-DECISIONS D1).

column1: bare-lease
column7: Three unrelated objects share the word. Say capability lease / containment lease / contingency lease. EXEMPTION `lease:` covers the capability_id token form `lease:{hunt}:{action}:{ms}` (22-DEMO-FIXTURE.md amendment C-A3), which is an identifier, not prose.

column1: bare-lane
column7: 'lane' means one of the twelve threat-class channels and nothing else. Use queue / pillar / stream (brief A9). EXEMPTION: the standalone nav/heading label. APPENDIX-NORMATIVE.md section 1 ratifies the routes /lanes and /lanes/$laneId, whose sidebar item and page heading are the bare word "Lanes" -- naming exactly the twelve threat-class channels the ruling permits. Anchored to the WHOLE string so it exempts a label and never a sentence: "open the async lane" still fails.

column1: exclamation
column7: Voice law L3: no exclamation marks, ever. The single permitted intensifier is the word "still". EXEMPTION: a literal that is ENTIRELY an HTML comment carrying no other `!`. The seven `<!-- swarm:<slug>:v1 -->` markers are wire literals the product must carry verbatim (APPENDIX-NORMATIVE.md section 3), and `<!--` contains a `!`, so without this the ban fires on every marker constant. Anchored and `[^!]*`-bounded so `<!-- Great news! -->` still fails. Found by scanning this artifact set's own fixtures.
